title: rollbackable-fallback-bridge-for-tenant-slo-safeguard
author: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Context: We observed repeated transient SLO pressure in regional clusters when a small subset of high-throughput tenants hit sudden bursts. Existing regional fallback heuristics could route to slower model variants but had two operational gaps: (1) partial rollouts into fallback paths left KV caches inconsistent and required a manual drain/rollback, (2) there was no safe, automated rollback path if the fallback made quality regressions.

This change introduces a rollbackable fallback bridge: a tenant-scoped, reversible reroute mechanism that (a) switches select tenant traffic to warm standby capacity inside the same region, (b) preserves and synchronizes KV cache state during the switch, and (c) records a rollback plan that the controller can apply atomically if quality or cost regressions are detected. The bridge is intentionally conservative: it only activates when SLO headroom crosses a configured threshold and when the tenant has opt-in fallback policy.

What I changed: implemented bridge controller in the serving runtime, added persisted fallback state in tenant metadata, added a lightweight pause-and-drain sequence for KV caches, and introduced telemetry hooks + alert rules to detect fallback regressions. Also added a canary rollout script and a runbook describing rollback steps.

Design notes: the fallback route is implemented as an admission-time rewrite that tags requests with a fallback header and routes via the existing steering mesh; we avoid two-phase commit across KV stores by using a short TTL sticky key (fallback:session) that is written to standby nodes during a 30s overlap window. The controller guarantees an eventual consistent state and exposes an emergency-rollback API that replays the recorded rollback plan (drain -> reattach -> invalidate sticky keys) to return traffic to primary capacity.

Risk/rollback: the change is guarded behind a feature-flag and tenant policy gate. Rollback is supported by a documented automated plan and a manual runbook. We instrumented metrics to detect quality delta and per-tenant cost delta and will auto-revert if thresholds are exceeded during canary.

Testing and rollout: unit tests for the controller and KV overlap logic, integration tests covering canary and rollback flows, and a staged canary that ramps to 5 tenants then 20% region traffic. CI runs include a synthetic SLO stress harness.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for bridge controller and sticky-key TTL handling
- [x] Integration tests for canary + rollback flow
- [x] Telemetry metrics and alert rules added
- [x] Runbook and KB article (docs/runbooks/fallback-rollback.md)
- [x] Feature flag gating and tenant opt-in policy
- [x] Canary deployment script + smoke checks

Related: ENG-2145 (tenant surge playbook), ENG-3387 (kv-drift-inspection).
commits: feat(runtime): add fallback bridge controller and admission hook
test(runtime): add unit tests for overlap drain and sticky key TTL
chore(ci): add canary-deploy script to CI pipeline
docs: add runbook for fallback rollback and KB article
telemetry: register fallback.bridge_activation and fallback.rollback_rate metrics
release_notes: Introduce rollbackable tenant fallback bridge: opt-in tenant reroute to standby capacity with atomic rollback plan and KV overlap drain. Guarded by feature flag. Improves reliability during tenant spikes while providing a safe rollback path for quality regressions.
review_comments: Miguel Torres: Overall looks good. Please add a late-bound feature flag to prevent accidental activation in Dedicated clusters.
Aisha Kapoor: Added feature flag check and gated default to 'off' for Dedicated in tenant_policy.go (see commit feat(flags)).
Lena Schmidt: Integration tests flaky on first run — observed race in sticky_key_store when TTL expired during overlap window. Suggest increase TTL or retry semantics.
Aisha Kapoor: Increased overlap window from 20s to 30s and added exponential retry to sticky key write. Added deterministic timing in test harness to reduce flakiness.
Omar Haddad: Telemetry looks useful; can we emit a delta metric for estimate cost delta per tenant during fallback? We should avoid counting duplicate tokens when requests are proxied.
Aisha Kapoor: Added fallback.estimated_cost_delta metric and dedup logic in router_rewrite. Also updated alert thresholds in infra/alerts/fallback_alerts.yaml.
ci_checks: integration-tests: initial failure (sticky_key_store race) -> rerun -> pass
merge_details: Merged by Miguel Torres via squash and merge on 2026-02-18. Commit message: feat(runtime): rollbackable fallback bridge (squashed). Post-merge: triggered canary pipeline and synthetic SLO stress job.
notes_for_ops: Ops: this feature is disabled by default. To enable for a tenant set tenant.policy.fallback.enabled=true and tenant.policy.fallback.threshold=0.72. Canary runbook documented in docs/runbooks/fallback-rollback.md; follow automated rollback steps if telemetry reports quality_delta>0.03 or cost_delta>0.25 for 10m.
changelog_entry: 2026-02-18: rollbackable tenant fallback bridge added behind feature flag; canary rollout scheduled. See runbook for rollback steps.
notes: This implementation prioritizes safe rollback and operational visibility over maximal throughput improvement. Next iteration will evaluate pre-warming standby caches proactively and integrating with Dedicated autoscaler policies.
